# Matting models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

13 matting models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image (trimap-guided models also a trimap: background / unknown / foreground). Output: an alpha matte `[H, W]` in [0, 1] at the input size: 1 = foreground (background removal, dichotomous / salient object segmentation).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 1080x1920: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured. The accuracy column is lower-is-better (DIS-VD MAE).

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## BEN2

BEN2 (Prama LLC, 2025): cuts the foreground out of a photo as a soft mask (background removal); a Swin Transformer looks at the whole image and at four full-resolution patches and merges the views. MIT code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ben2` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 201<br>110<br>104<br>103<br>58.2 | 2466 / 2772<br>1681 / 1976<br>1942 / 2238<br>813 / 916<br>1280 / 1326 |

## BiRefNet

BiRefNet (Nankai University and partners, CAAI AIR 2024): cuts the foreground out of a photo as a soft mask at full resolution (background removal), with a Swin Transformer encoder; general and lite versions (MIT code and weights) and BRIA's RMBG-2.0 weights (non-commercial, gated download).

Commercial use: `birefnet`, `birefnet-lite`: yes; `rmbg-2.0`: **no** (weights: CC-BY-NC-4.0).

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `birefnet` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 234<br>131<br>121<br>138<br>87.8 | 1666 / 1930<br>1660 / 1908<br>1674 / 1916<br>1874 / 1932<br>1753 / 1814 |

| `rmbg-2.0` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 149<br>132<br>121<br>110<br>88.1 | 1672 / 1990<br>1660 / 1908<br>1674 / 1936<br>1874 / 1932<br>1723 / 1784 |

## InSPyReNet

InSPyReNet (Kim et al., ACCV 2022) as transparent-background ships it: cuts the foreground out of a photo as a soft mask at 1024 x 1024 (384 x 384 fast); a Swin-B encoder with an image-pyramid decoder. MIT code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inspyrenet` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 241<br>109<br>–<br>85.8<br>fails: TensorRT: NaN output (onnxruntime on the same ONNX is right) | 3240 / 3262<br>1649 / 1848<br>–<br>913 / 1018<br>– |
| `inspyrenet-fast` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 71.1<br>41.7<br>–<br>17.7<br>6.99 | 810 / 836<br>432 / 488<br>–<br>345 / 376<br>561 / 600 |

- Authors' code, not used: <https://github.com/plemeri/InSPyReNet> (PyTorch): fastforks follows the authors' transparent-background package, which ships the released InSPyReNet weights (Plus_Ultra) and the inference call that ComfyUI nodes use, rather than the research repository.

## IS-Net

Commercial use: yes.

## U²-Net

U²-Net (University of Alberta, Pattern Recognition 2020): finds the main object of a photo and cuts it out as a soft mask at 320 x 320 (rembg's default background remover); a full model, a 4.7 MB small one and one trained on people. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |

| `u2netp` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 14.8<br>14.6<br>9.80<br>5.44<br>1.87 | 280 / 314<br>150 / 172<br>138 / 172<br>152 / 188<br>206 / 236 |

<a id="vitmatte"></a>

## ViTMatte

ViTMatte (Huazhong University of Science and Technology, 2023): refines a rough trimap (sure background, sure foreground, unknown band) into a soft alpha matte, e.g. hair and fur edges; a plain Vision Transformer plus a small detail decoder; small and base versions. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vitmatte-s` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 140<br>102<br>83.8<br>81.9<br>54.6 | 2536 / 2582<br>1401 / 1524<br>1337 / 1444<br>1025 / 1284<br>876 / 920 |
| `vitmatte-b` | synthetic (1080x1920) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 257<br>182<br>147<br>157<br>108 | 5070 / 5128<br>1548 / 1692<br>1484 / 1710<br>1166 / 1472<br>1233 / 1262 |
